title: Thinking on Being Successful with Samhita Arni
summary: Kahran talks with writer Samhita Arni — who published her first NY Times bestseller at age 11 — about whether early success ever stops following you and how she's trying to redefine success now. They go into her transcultural childhood as the daughter of an Indian intelligence officer, her four years studying to be a psychotherapist, how she moved back to Bangalore to care for her grandmother with Alzheimer's, and her practice of Ira Progoff's depth journaling.
topics: moving back to care for an aging grandmother
feeling like an imposter in your mother tongue

intents.display: to hear a child-prodigy writer rethink what success means in her 30s
to think about depth journaling and a creative routine
